review: REST is the verb remain inactive. STIR means begin moving, not mix a drink or provoke an emotion; MOVE and ACT mean be active and perform action. STIRRED is its ordinary past tense, keeping the same verb type. All accepted inflections must retain these activity senses. STRIDE, TRAVEL, ROVE, RIDE, TREAD, GO and RISE all use physical movement, contrasting remaining inactive and still. STIRED is blocked as a malformed inflection; STIR requires two Rs in STIRRED. The R armour needs two copies. Independent review adds ARISE, AROUSE, ROAM, GLIDE, DART, TRUDGE, SLIDE, RACE, ROUSE, SOAR, SURGE, SCURRY and DRIVE in exact literal movement/activity senses. GOES and DOES restore ordinary verb inflections missing from the catalog, not the game or deer nouns.
